headline: Export licences-related setbacks begin to taper off

highlights: Anand Rathi Research India Equities India I Equities Aniket Jain Research Analyst Capital Goods Result Update 4 November 2026 Jyoti CNC Automation Export licences-related setbacks begin to taper off; maintain BUY The company’s financials continued to be impacted in Q2FY27, led by export license-related issues at Huron, which impacted consolidated revenues and EBITDA.
The management is confident of clocking in sales of ~Rs3bn in FY27, implying Rs2-2.25bn sales in H2FY27e.
Orders increased 30% y/y in Q2FY27 to Rs8.09bn, taking the OB to Rs50.82bn, providing visibility for the next 18-20 months.
With the machine dispatches increasing by 44% y/y to a record 1,911, we expect the machine deliveries to improve further, as the new capacity ramps up.
valuation: Accordingly, we maintain BUY rating on the stock with a TP of Rs1,275, valuing it at 40x Sep-28e TTM EPS, which implies ~31% upside from the current level.
Outlook and Valuation: We continue to expect 30% revenue CAGR over FY26-29e, aided by OB of >Rs50bn.
Guidance ◼ It targets to deliver 8,000 machines and expects order worth Rs25-30bn.
watch: Outlook and Valuation: We continue to expect 30% revenue CAGR over FY26-29e, aided by OB of >Rs50bn.
Key Risks: (a) Revenue deferral due to delay in grant of export licences; (b) elevated working capital; and (c) elongated supply chain issues.
